name: Listbox
description: A widget that presents a list of options allowing users to select one or more, communicating option names, states, and positions to assistive technologies.

keyboard_interactions.action: Moves focus to next option matching typed character(s)
Moves focus and toggles selection of next option
Moves focus and toggles selection of previous option

optional_attributes.description: true for multi-select; omit for single-select
true for selected; false for unselectable
horizontal for horizontal arrangement; default is vertical
Total options when not all in DOM

notes: Use <select>. It is complete, and on mobile it gets the native picker. Build the ARIA listbox only for rich option markup or multi-select UX a <select multiple> cannot express.
Two focus models are valid: roving tabindex (real focus moves to the option) or aria-activedescendant (focus stays on the listbox container). Pick ONE. Mixing them is the defining bug.
With aria-activedescendant you must scrollIntoView the active option yourself — there is no real focus to scroll to.
aria-setsize/aria-posinset are only needed when the DOM does not contain every option (virtualised lists). Otherwise the browser counts them for you.
Type-ahead (jump to the option starting with the typed letter) is expected behaviour and free with <select>.
For a listbox inside a combobox, see patterns/combobox.md — the wiring differs.

raweb_criteria.reason: listbox/option roles and aria-selected must be exposed; no native semantics apply to a div-built listbox.
Arrow keys must traverse options; the widget must be operable by keyboard and pointer alike.
It sets a form value, so it needs a label — aria-labelledby pointing at a visible one.
With aria-activedescendant the option has no real focus, so :focus-visible never fires — you must style [aria-selected] yourself.
Roving tabindex or aria-activedescendant must keep the listbox a single, coherent Tab stop.
Tab must always leave the listbox.
